title: Measure cut and join our pouch
outcome: TEXTILES: measure, cut and join accurately.
goal: I can use my checked design to measure, cut and join accurately with safe support.
success: I can mark and check two pieces before cutting.
I can use the agreed cutting and joining method safely.
I can check an actual measurement and record a useful change.
brief: Make a small reusable pouch to hold three paper prompt cards, each 60 mm by 80 mm. Leave the top open. Join the sides and bottom. It should hold the cards upright, have no loose sharp parts and be comfortable to handle.
dimensions: Default plan: two pieces, each 100 mm wide by 120 mm high. This is 10 cm by 12 cm. Mark a seam line 10 mm inside the left, right and bottom edges. Keep the top open. Use the pupil’s actual approved Week 4 design if it differs.
steps: Retrieve your actual Week 4 design. Measure from the ruler’s zero mark, not its end. Mark two 100 mm by 120 mm rectangles. Recheck each side and mark 10 mm seam lines on the left, right and bottom.

An adult checks the marks before cutting. Keep fingers outside the blade path. Use agreed fabric scissors under the agreed supervision. Turn the fabric rather than reaching across the blades. Put scissors down when you stop.

Lay the two pieces together with the edges aligned. The adult selects a suitable needle and thread for the actual fabric. Pass thread through the needle eye and tie a small tail knot, or use a prepared threaded needle. Start between the layers and bring the needle out through the upper layer at the seam guide so the knot stays inside.

Follow the marked line through both layers. Move about 5 mm along the line and put the needle through both layers. Bring it back through both layers about 5 mm further along. Keep fingers clear of the exit point. Pull gently away from faces so the thread lies flat. Repeat small even passes along the left, bottom and right lines. Leave the top open.

On the back, take a small stitch through both layers and leave a loop before pulling tight. Pass the needle through the loop and pull snug. Repeat once. An adult demonstrates this and helps as needed. Trim thread only with agreed scissors. Count and return every needle to its container.
safety: Adult checks actual design, tools, fabric and access needs before issuing equipment.
Use scissors and needles only with agreed adult supervision. Keep fingers clear of blade and needle exit points.
Count needles before and after. Keep them in a container. Never put needles or pins in your mouth or leave them in the pouch.

Pause with tools down and work safe. Stop for a missing or broken needle and keep the area clear. The adult recovers and accounts for every part and controls disposal. Do not release the pouch until all sharps are accounted for.
If bonding was chosen, use only adult-approved fabric adhesive after actual label checks. Follow its full cure time. No heat, irons or solvents are used in this lesson.
fallback: With no fabric or safe tools, use a paper model or empty-hand rehearsal. Mark imagined measurements, explain the cut line and trace the running stitch route. Record this as planning or simulation. Keep textile measuring, cutting and joining evidence pending until those actions happen on actual fabric with approved tools.
bonding: Use an adhesive route only if it is in the actual approved design and the adult has checked the fabric, product label, ventilation and access needs. Follow that label for application and full cure time. Do not invent a curing time or test an uncured join. No heat or solvents are used. Keep joining or testing pending where needed.

Supported: Use one action at a time with an adult.
Point to the ruler zero and the 100 mm and 120 mm marks.
Complete or direct the agreed cut and join. Ask for prepared pieces if needed.
Check one real measurement and record what you and the adult each did.
Standard: Check your Week 4 design and mark both pieces.
Recheck the marks before using the approved cutting method.
Follow the demonstrated join and keep the top open.
Measure the actual pieces and seam line. Record a correction and support.
Stretch: Complete the core making and accuracy check first.
Compare planned and actual measurements on both pieces.
Explain how an even join and flat thread help the pouch meet its purpose.
Justify a real correction or identify one change for the next making session.

vocabulary: Find a length using the ruler scale.
Show a line or point before cutting or joining.
The line where pieces of fabric are joined.
Small passes of thread through both layers along a line.
How close an actual result is to the planned measure.
Allow an adhesive to set fully as its label directs.

adaptations.Cognition and Learning: Show one measure or stitch action at a time. Model from ruler zero, then fade the next check. Use the same units throughout. Offer a marked guide, prepared pieces or a repeated checklist, recording support honestly.
adaptations.Communication and Interaction: Accept pointing, speech, signing and pupil-directed adult handling. Give one short instruction and thinking time. Read the recorded account back for the pupil to correct.
adaptations.SEMH: Offer a calm pause with tools down and needles counted or safely contained. Agree a short return cue. Keep the accuracy check about improving the work, not judging the pupil. Use private adult feedback if preferred.
adaptations.Sensory and Physical: Offer an approved adapted tool, prepared pieces, a threaded needle or pupil-directed adult handling. Check actual fabric sensitivities privately. Use a large clear ruler view. No sharp tool is issued until the adult approves the route.
adaptations.EAL: Rehearse in any language. Pair the ruler value, unit and action word. Check the meaning of through both layers and top open before tools are issued. Use confirmed scribing where needed.

careers: Textile makers use measurements, safe tools and repeat checks to turn a design into a useful item. Accurate records help another person understand a change.

stages.name: Arrival
stages.title: Our actual design
pupil: Find your Week 4 design decision.
Confirm the fabric and join with the adult.
Wait for approved tools and support.
stages.teacher: Retrieve actual designs. Confirm purpose, fabric, dimensions and technique before issuing tools. If the design is missing, agree the supplied default plan today and label that new decision honestly. Check access, supervision, tool condition and needle count. A non-specialist cover adult uses prepared pieces or pupil-directed handling unless approved and competent to supervise the cutting and sewing.
stages.check: Ask: What must this pouch hold? Expect three 60 mm by 80 mm cards upright. Confirm the actual approved design, rather than assuming every pupil chose felt or stitching.

stages.name: Starter
stages.title: Ruler zero and the units
pupil: Point to zero on the ruler.
Show 100 mm and 120 mm.
Find the 10 mm seam margin.
stages.teacher: Model the zero mark and explain that a ruler’s physical end may sit before zero. Read 100 mm as 10 cm and 120 mm as 12 cm. Keep millimetres as the working unit. Show the three joined edges and the open top.
stages.check: Ask whether 10 mm equals 1 cm or 10 cm. Correct is 1 cm. Revisit the marked scale if units are mixed.

stages.name: I do
stages.title: A checked cut and running stitch
pupil: Watch measure, mark and recheck.
See how the needle goes through both layers.
Watch the flat thread and secure end.
stages.teacher: Use the measuring card and join steps. Demonstrate a checked mark and a short cut with the locally approved scissor method. Then align layers, thread and knot an appropriate needle, start between layers and show small running stitch passes about 5 mm apart along the seam line. Keep fingers clear of the exit point. Pull the thread flat, not tight enough to pucker. Show the securing loop twice and safe tool return. Model one pass, then invite the pupil to explain the next action before handling a tool.
stages.check: Ask: Do we join only one layer or both? Expect both layers on the marked line. If unclear, demonstrate through two prepared layers again before pupil sewing.

stages.name: We do
stages.title: Mark and check together
pupil: Measure and mark two pieces from your plan.
Recheck all four sides before cutting.
Mark the three 10 mm seam lines.
stages.teacher: Guide the first ruler placement, then fade support on the second. Check each rectangle is 100 by 120 mm under the default plan. Mark the left, right and bottom seam lines 10 mm inside the edge; leave the top open. Adult approves before cutting. Cut in the agreed way, or let the pupil direct adult cutting. Align pieces and keep scrap away from needle work.
stages.check: A mark made from the ruler end instead of zero is remeasured. Record actual marks and support; a printed diagram is not a cutting template or a measurement record.

stages.name: We do 2
stages.title: The accuracy hinge
pupil: The plan says 100 mm. A cut piece is 103 mm.
Is it within the 2 mm check range?
Stop and agree a safe correction.
stages.teacher: Correct answer is no: the width range is 98 to 102 mm. A 103 mm piece is 3 mm too wide. Remeasure from zero, then discuss whether a safe trim is suitable before joining. Parallel check: a seam line is 7 mm from the edge; the 10 mm target range is 8 to 12 mm, so re-mark before sewing. If either check is missed, return to the ruler and use paired checks before continuing. These are improvement checks, not pupil grades.
stages.check: All pupils can point to the relevant planned and actual values or explain the difference before proceeding. An adult decides whether trimming is safe and still meets the actual design.

stages.name: Independent
stages.title: Join the actual pieces
pupil: Align the two pieces.
Use the agreed join along three sides.
Keep the top open and check the thread lies flat.
stages.teacher: Pupils make the approved join with ongoing adult supervision. The timetable label does not mean unsupervised needle or scissor use. Use small even running stitches through both layers. If the actual design chose bonding, use only the cleared label-led route and keep cure or testing pending until complete. A pupil can direct adult handling. Record the real amount completed and support. Stop safely if time runs out.
stages.check: Look for both layers joined along the marked route, open top, safe tool actions and actual pupil role. Do not claim independent sewing where the adult sewed.

stages.name: Review
stages.title: My accuracy self check
pupil: Put tools down and return counted needles.
Record actual width, height and seam margin.
Name one correction or next step.
stages.teacher: Collect and count all needles first. Record actual measurements on the accuracy card. Compare default width and height with the 2 mm ranges and seam margin with 8 to 12 mm. A revised design uses its own recorded target. Inspect for flat thread and gaps. Keep unfinished work, uncured joins and unsafe or unperformed actions honest. Agree how the item is stored for Week 6.
stages.check: A checked number needs a real measurement, units and support. If a pupil used prepared pieces, separate their checking from the adult’s cutting.

stages.name: Exit
stages.title: My making record
pupil: I measured or directed ___.
My actual join is ___.
Next time I need to finish or improve ___.
stages.teacher: Keep the actual item, design reference, measurements, join stage, support and next step together. Let the pupil correct any scribed words. Week 6 finishes and evaluates the product. No weekly outcome or practical skill is awarded from simulation alone.
stages.check: The record distinguishes pupil action, adult action, actual textile work and simulation. Missing evidence remains pending.

misconceptions: The ruler end is always zero.
Find and align the printed zero mark before reading the length.
A fastening joins the sides of the pouch.
Fastenings close an opening. The left, right and bottom still need their agreed join.
Pulling thread hard makes the join better.
Pull gently away from faces so the thread lies flat. Too much tension can gather or pucker the fabric.
A paper model proves textile making.
Label the model as simulation and keep textile practical evidence pending.
